reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that impulses generate affective feedback loops—pleasure upon completion, pain upon interruption—regardless of the original motive. This forms a dual-valued motivational tensor where each action is evaluated not only by its goal but also by how well it resolves within a given context. The tensor components are defined by the interplay of impulse strength (A), external forces (F), and resulting affective states (P, U). In GSI, these map into Bayesian belief networks over action outcomes, where prior motives are updated based on affective feedback. In GSE, they define a state transition system where actions are selected to maximize expected pleasure while minimizing disruption pain. The dual nature of these feedbacks creates a non-linear control structure, where the same impulse can be both a driver and a constraint depending on environmental resistance. Failure modes include misalignment between pursued and incidental pleasures, leading to suboptimal behavior or affective dysregulation.
